walkthroughs.body_html:
Between 1577 and 1580 Francis Drake sailed round the world in the Golden Hind.

He raided Spanish ports and treasure ships. Elizabeth knighted him on his return — angering Philip II of Spain. Drake captured £140,000 of Spanish silver — twice the Crown's annual income.

The 1585 Treaty of Nonsuch sent English troops to help Dutch Protestants against Spain.

In 1587 Drake raided Cadiz — burning 30 ships and delaying the Armada a year. Philip II planned invasion to restore Catholicism and avenge Mary's execution.

Philip's fleet of 130 ships sailed from Lisbon in May 1588.

It reached Calais but met English fireships in the night. The Battle of Gravelines (8 August 1588) scattered it. Storms — the Protestant Wind — wrecked the ships round Scotland and Ireland. Only 67 returned home.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.

mcqs.q: What were the Wars of the Roses really about?
options: Dynastic conflict between rival branches of the Plantagenets (Lancaster and York) over the throne, intensified by weak kingship under Henry VI and noble factionalism.
The whole country was at war for thirty continuous years.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
